task: Section 13: Compile: Seed -> Seed; test Compile(R*) ~ R*; distinguish dynamical fixed point from compiler fixed point; record missing information if any.
compile_definition_used: Compile := Gamma_infty (the iterated color-refinement quotient operator, the only structure-derived operator constructed in this run -- see seed_candidate_registry.json Candidate D). No alternative 'Compile' operator was independently motivated by source material or by the finite mathematics tested, so Compile and Gamma_infty are treated as the same object in this run; this identification is flagged explicitly rather than assumed silently.

dynamical_vs_compiler_fixed_point.dynamical_fixed_point_Type_IV: R* such that iterating R_{n+1}=F(R_n) from R_0=R* stays at R* (up to isomorphism) for all n.
dynamical_vs_compiler_fixed_point.relationship_found: Under the identification Compile:=Gamma_infty, these two notions COINCIDE exactly for this run's operator: Gamma_infty was constructed BY iterating quotient-and-refine to convergence, so a single application of Gamma_infty already equals what repeated application would give (idempotence, numerically verified with zero exceptions across all 3160 isomorphism classes tested at N=1..4 -- see seed_relation_iso.json, gamma_infty_idempotence_failures=0 at every N). Type IV and Type V are therefore EQUIVALENT under this run's specific realization, though the task's own definitions (section 3) do not force this in general -- a different, non-idempotent Compile operator could separate them.

missing_information_check.question: Does Compile(R*) require information not contained in R* itself?
missing_information_check.finding: NO. Gamma_infty is defined purely as a function of R's own adjacency structure (iterated color-refinement, using only R's edges) -- it requires no externally supplied seed, target, or parameter. This was verified computationally: the SAME function color_refinement(bits, N), taking only the relation's own bit-representation and size, was applied uniformly to every one of the 2+10+104+3044 isomorphism classes with no per-instance external input.
missing_information_check.one_caveat_recorded: The STOPPING CRITERION for iteration (section 20's Gamma_infty loop) is a generic property of ANY finite monotonically-shrinking sequence (vertex count is bounded below by 1 and strictly decreases on every non-fixed step) -- this is a general mathematical fact about finite sets, not information imported from outside R. No missing information was identified.

important_negative_finding.claim_tested: Is the naive ONE-SHOT color-refinement operator (Gamma_1, a single pass of 1-WL refinement with no re-quotienting) itself a valid 'Compile' in the Type V sense?
important_negative_finding.result: NO -- Gamma_1 is NOT idempotent in general. 4 of 104 isomorphism classes at N=3 and 59 of 3044 at N=4 have a Gamma_1-quotient that, when independently re-refined from a blank initial coloring, collapses FURTHER (a concrete N=3 example is reproduced in the closure report: the twin pair {0,1} in a 3-vertex relation collapses to a 2-vertex quotient that is itself perfectly symmetric, and a fresh 1-WL run on that 2-vertex quotient cannot break the symmetry, collapsing it again to 1 vertex). This is because 1-WL color refinement can never distinguish two vertices related by a nontrivial automorphism of the CURRENT graph, and a freshly-quotiented graph can itself possess new automorphisms invisible to the original graph's refinement history. Practical consequence: a 'Compile' implemented as one-shot color refinement is NOT a well-defined idempotent compiler; Gamma_infty (iterate to convergence) is required for Type V to hold. This distinction is preserved explicitly in the theorem registry (THM-SEED-FIXEDPOINT-001) rather than silently patched over.
important_negative_finding.importantly_this_does_not_change_the_fix: Because no collapse step can ever increase vertex count, a relation with ZERO collapse on the first pass (Gamma_1(R)~R) is automatically also a true Gamma_infty fixed point, and vice versa -- verified exactly: 2/2, 6/6, 70/70, 2462/2462 at N=1,2,3,4 respectively. The Gamma_1 vs Gamma_infty distinction affects only relations that DO collapse (the trajectory taken to reach the true fixed point of a non-fixed R), not which relations count as seeds.
